newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares lacklustre in early Friday trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares lacklustre in early Friday trade.

text.p: Singapore shares opened relaxed on Friday as lacklustre Christmas week trade continued, dealers said.
"We've got a lot of holidays at this time of year and into next week, so I wouldn't think there would be anything moving the market," said a local dealer.
Leisure and cinema sectors were holding most market interest as traders reflected on what else they could have been doing on such a quiet trading week, said the dealer.
Nevertheless, there was upward movement on the key Straits Times Industrials Index, up 2.77 at 2,200.46 at 0230 GMT.
But wafer thin volume of 4.8 million shares traded in the market's first 90 minutes painted the underlying picture of uninspired inactivity.

UOB Bank, the share which could have moved well on Thursday's forecasts that merging its Malaysian banking operations would assist growth and boost profits, was up only Singapore $0.05, but that still made it early trading's seventh biggest gainer.
Gainers at 0430 GMT were headed by Creative Technology, up S$0.40 to S$13.20. Losers were led by Malaysia's Innovest Bhd, down S$0.12 at S$4.72.
